chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abu al-Khattab narrated to us, from Nasr ibn Muzahim, from Umar ibn Sa'd, from Amr ibn Thabit, from Habib ibn Abu Thabit, from Umm Salama, wife of the Prophet (may Allah's blessings be upon him and his family):

She said: I had not heard the wailing of the jinn since the Prophet (may Allah's blessings be upon him and his family) was taken until this night, and I do not see myself except that I have been afflicted with my son. She said: And a jinniyyah from among them came saying: Lo! O eye, shed tears strenuously, for who shall weep over the martyrs after me -- over a clan whom death is leading towards a despot in the kingdom of a slave.

key_terms.الشهداء: The martyrs -- referring to Imam Husayn and his companions at Karbala
key_terms.نوح الجن: The wailing of the jinn -- referring to the supernatural mourning by jinn over the martyrdom of Husayn

ai.seo_question: Did the jinn mourn the martyrdom of Imam Husayn at Karbala according to Umm Salama?
ai.summary: Umm Salama, wife of the Prophet (S), reports that she had not heard the wailing of the jinn since the Prophet was taken until that night, and she believed her son had been struck. Then a female jinn came reciting poetry mourning the martyrs, lamenting: O eye, shed tears strenuously, for who shall weep over the martyrs after me -- over a clan whom death leads towards a despot in the kingdom of a slave. This narration connects the supernatural realm of the jinn to the mourning of Imam Husayn at Karbala, showing that even jinn recognized and grieved the enormity of this tragedy.
